A_target.statement:
Let $L$ be a [[Definition:Regular Language|regular language]].
Then $L$ has a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] (up to [[Definition:Isomorphism|isomorphism]]) [[Definition:Minimal Deterministic Finite Automaton|minimal deterministic finite automaton]], given by:
:$M_{\min} = M / \sim$
where $M$ is any [[Definition:Deterministic Finite Automaton|DFA]] for $L$ with all states reachable and $\sim$ is [[Definition:Indistinguishable States|indistinguishability]] of states.

B_source.statement:
Let $f: A \to B$ be a [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|homomorphism]] of [[Definition:Algebraic Structure|algebraic structures]].
Then:
:$A / \map \ker f \cong \Img f$

substitutions.the structure-preserving map: the map sending a state to the set of suffixes it accepts

derived.the image: the set of residual languages of the language

object_map.reformulation: State minimality must be reformulated as a statement about residual languages before the kernel-quotient pattern applies.

validity_conditions: all states must be reachable, or unreachable states must be removed first, since they are invisible to the map
the indistinguishability relation must be a congruence with respect to the transition function for the quotient to be an automaton
the automaton must be deterministic and complete for the residual-language map to be well defined
proof_plan:
Delete all states of $M$ not reachable from the [[Definition:Initial State|initial state]].
This does not change the accepted [[Definition:Formal Language|language]].

Define $\rho$ on states by:
:$\map \rho q = \set {w \in \Sigma^*: \map {\delta^*} {q, w} \in F}$
the [[Definition:Residual Language|residual language]] accepted from $q$.

For each $a \in \Sigma$:
:$\map \rho {\map \delta {q, a} } = a^{-1} \map \rho q$
Hence the [[Definition:Equivalence Relation|equivalence]] $q \sim q' \iff \map \rho q = \map \rho {q'}$ is a [[Definition:Congruence Relation|congruence]] for the transitions.
Form the [[Definition:Quotient Automaton|quotient automaton]] $M / \sim$ by merging states with the same residual language.

By the pattern of the [[First Isomorphism Theorem]], $M / \sim$ is isomorphic to the image of $\rho$, the automaton of residual languages of $L$.
By the [[Myhill-Nerode Theorem]], this automaton has the minimum number of states and depends only on $L$.
Hence the minimal DFA is [[Definition:Unique|unique]] up to renaming of states.
{{qed}}
